collection.description: The village swing makes an odd sound only when the youngest children use it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The village swing makes an odd sound only when the youngest children use it.

choices.label: Ask the Children What They Notice
Let Children Demonstrate from the Ground
Find a New Game While Waiting

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: They explain that the sound happens when feet brush a loose reed below the seat.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: One child notices that the swing twists before it squeaks, prompting an adult safety check.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: Adults find a fraying cord and repair it before anyone rides again.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: The cords are sound, but the children point out a branch rubbing the frame.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: (child) reproduces the squeak with a stick while everyone stays off the swing.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: The sound disappears, and the children suggest checking again after the afternoon breeze.

text_only.reason: the word's everyday sense (an animal, a sound, a thing or a mark out of sight); nobody leaves the village -- the volume's outcomes are story text unless an effect is marked

d2.name: Outcome D2
d2.text: (child), a disappointed child, helps paint a temporary closed sign and feels included in the decision.

d1__fx.name: Outcome D1
d1__fx.text: The children invent a ground-level jumping game that becomes unexpectedly popular.
